key_insight: Transformer architecture is a major driver of performance in continuous diffusion language models, and LangDiT improves generation quality by tailoring normalization, conditioning, routing, and self-conditioning to the CDLM setting.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a plug-and-play backbone upgrade for continuous language generators that improves perplexity without changing the underlying representation, objective, or sampler.
method: Combine feature normalization with query-key normalization for CDLM-specific stability.
Expand noise conditioning and add likelihood-shortcut gradient routing plus calibration.
Use confidence-gated training self-conditioning to improve denoising behavior.
evidence_signal: Across matched evaluations on OpenWebText 1024-token unconditional generation, LangDiT reaches state-of-the-art GenPPL, including 21.72 at 1024 NFEs and 44.72 at 128 NFEs in LangFlow, and 11.33 at 1024 denoising NFEs and 27.51 at 128 NFEs in Plaid-style formulations.
watch_item: The gains are demonstrated on continuous diffusion language model setups and may depend on careful integration with the chosen CDLM formulation and inference budget.
paper_title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
